trust_decision.summary: ndsudo (setuid root, executable by group netdata) lets its caller supply the {{socket_path}} template value, which fail2ban-client runs as root then connects to; the fix makes ndsudo's command table hard-code the socket path, so the caller no longer decides it.

landing_point.why: The summary names ndsudo and socket_path; the fail2ban-client-status-socket entry in allowed_commands is the only place where {{socket_path}} is templated.

fix_sites.module_kind: privileged setuid helper (C), command allow-list table
privileged setuid helper (C), command allow-list table
unprivileged Go caller / wrapper of ndsudo
unprivileged Go caller / wrapper of ndsudo

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/go/plugin/go.d/collector/fail2ban/exec.go:19 and src/go/plugin/go.d/collector/fail2ban/exec.go:45-57 (the Go collector that supplies --socket_path; the fix moves the constant from here into ndsudo)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 routes: 'the advisory is about fail2ban's pickle socket; varnishstat/smartctl/nvme/intel_gpu_top only read devices or stats, so their caller-supplied paths are a different feature and not a deserialisation sink.' For the O2 site: 'the Go caller always passes a constant, so it is not the attack surface.'

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Docker mode must still query the host fail2ban socket at /host/var/run/fail2ban/fail2ban.sock, and the caller-supplied {{jail}} name must keep working. Other ndsudo commands that legitimately take caller values ({{deviceName}}, {{device}}, {{options}}, {{interval}}, {{devname}}) must keep working too. A fix that drops the -socket commands, or strips all template substitution, breaks these.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: varnishstat-stats: the caller supplies -n {{instanceName}}, a varnish working-directory path whose shared-memory files varnishstat reads and parses as root
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a stats reader, not fail2ban, and not a pickle/socket client; the advisory names only socket_path
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and table, 90 lines above the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: smartctl-json-device-info: the caller-supplied {{deviceName}} is placed as a positional argument to root smartctl; any value (a path, or a string starting with '-', since check_string allows '-', '/' and '=') reaches smartctl's argv
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: device access is the command's purpose; a device path is needed for legitimate use

O8_uncovered_routes.route: nvme-smart-log: the caller-supplied {{device}} path is opened by root nvme-cli
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a device path is legitimately caller-chosen; no deserialisation

O8_uncovered_routes.route: igt-device-json: the caller-supplied {{device}} filter (which can name sysfs/drm paths) is passed to root intel_gpu_top -d
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: a GPU selection filter, a neighbouring feature

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new allow-list entry for another root-run client whose control socket, config or state path is a {{template}} value (for example a daemon-ctl -s {{socket}} stats entry)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The table already mixes fixed and caller-templated params, and a maintainer adding docker support would copy the fail2ban -socket pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a HOW-type parser differential: the variable lookup picks the first matching --name anywhere in argv, including the command-name position. A sibling that validates one occurrence and substitutes another would be realistic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: find_variable_in_argv scans argv from index 1 with no positional structure, so a validation step added elsewhere could easily disagree with it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a collector config option (instance_name) that flows to a path-typed ndsudo variable
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists, as a user-configured value that reaches a path argument of a root tool.

O9_family: privileged-helper argument trust: a caller-controlled external path (CWE-73) leads a root process to deserialise attacker data (CWE-502)

O10_build.toolchain: CMake + C compiler for ndsudo (CMakeLists.txt:2786-2790, a standalone single-file target); Go toolchain for go.d.plugin
O10_build.project_tests: src/go/plugin/go.d/collector/fail2ban/collector_test.go (mock CLI; does not reach ndsudo). The fix adds exec_test.go using ndexec.SetRunnerPathsForTests (src/go/plugin/go.d/pkg/ndexec/ndexec.go:124). No C tests for ndsudo were found; behaviour can be checked offline without root via 'ndsudo --test <cmd> ...' (src/collectors/utils/ndsudo.c:445-498).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate or whitelist socket_path inside ndsudo's check_string, or only change the Go caller's constant, instead of removing the caller-controlled socket template from the privileged table.

out_of_scope_notes: ndsudo --test with argc==2 reads argv[2] (NULL) into find_command (src/collectors/utils/ndsudo.c:445-450), a crash only.
ndsudo has a duplicate chronyc-serverstats entry (src/collectors/utils/ndsudo.c:26 and :79), harmless.
Other setuid helpers (cgroup-network, local-listeners, ioping) are installed with elevated perms (packaging/makeself/install-or-update.sh:235); they were not examined.

The defence counted for j_defence_ineffective is check_string (src/collectors/utils/ndsudo.c:297-312). It filters characters but allows '/' and '.', so arbitrary paths pass.
